record.paper_title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
record.original_question: Consider the linear Volterra functional integro-differential equation u'(t) = a u(t) + b u(qt) + \int_0^t k_0(t-s)u(s)\,ds + \int_0^{qt} k_1(t-s)u(s)\,ds for t \ge 0, where the corresponding pantograph equation without the integral terms is already asymptotically stable. For which continuous or weakly singular kernels k_0 and k_1 do the nontrivial solutions of this test equation still satisfy \lim_{t	o\infty} u(t)=0?

evidence.quote: For VFIDEs with vanishing delays we consider the linear test equation u'(t) = au(t) + bu(qt) + ∫ t 0 k0(t − s)u(s)ds + ∫ qt 0 k1(t − s)u(s)ds, t \ge 0. (4.8)

Open Problem 4.2 (a) Assume that the coefficients a and b in the pantograph equation (4.1) (or (4.4)) are such that its solution is asymptotically stable (i.e., assume (4.3) or (4.5)). Which (continuous, or weakly singular) convolution kernels k0 and k1 do nontrivial solutions of the linear test VFIDE (4.8) satisfy (4.2)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the linear scalar Volterra functional integro-differential test equation with a vanishing proportional delay
  u'(t) = a u(t) + b u(qt) + \int_0^t k_0(t-s) u(s)\,ds + \int_0^{qt} k_1(t-s) u(s)\,ds,  t \ge 0,
where a, b \in \mathbb{R}, q \in (0,1) is a fixed proportionality constant, u(0) = u_0 \in \mathbb{R}, and k_0, k_1 are real-valued convolution kernels defined on [0, \infty), assumed to be either continuous or weakly singular (i.e. of the form k_i(\tau) = \tau^{-\alpha_i} K_i(\tau) with 0 < \alpha_i < 1 and K_i continuous and bounded). Assume that the coefficients a and b are such that the underlying pantograph equation v'(t) = a v(t) + b v(qt), t \ge 0, is asymptotically stable, i.e. every solution v satisfies \lim_{t\to\infty} v(t) = 0.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the kernel pair (k_0, k_1) (within the continuous and the weakly singular classes) under which every nontrivial solution u of the integro-differential equation above still satisfies
  \lim_{t\to\infty} u(t) = 0.
artifact.category_tag: Volterra integro-differential equations with vanishing delays
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a survey on numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays. Subsequent work (e.g. studies on asymptotic stability of Volterra integral equations with vanishing delays via variation-of-parameters and energy methods, and on collocation stability for pantograph DDEs) addresses related cases, but no source found provides a complete characterization of admissible continuous or weakly singular kernels (k_0, k_1) for the full integro-differential test equation. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the asymptotic stability of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic stability of solutions of linear Volterra integral equations with general continuous convolution kernels and vanishing delays, via extension of variation-of-parameters and energy techniques.
status_evidence.claim: Related work treats the integral (non-differential) version with vanishing delays, but does not give a full characterization for the integro-differential test equation.

status_evidence.title: Stability of collocation methods for delay differential equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic stability of collocation solutions for linear DDEs with vanishing proportional delay qt is studied; A-stable ODE collocation methods inherit stability for the pantograph DDE.
status_evidence.claim: Existing stability results address the pantograph DDE part, not the combined VFIDE with both convolution integrals.

status_evidence.title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems including asymptotic stability of the test VFIDE u'(t)=au(t)+bu(qt)+∫k_0+∫k_1.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly stated as an open problem.
